test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

These tutorials are so elementary that they can help neither you nor I.
solution:
The correct sentence is- 'neither you nor I' ***__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the pronoun '*i*' is incorrectly used.
 
• We know that we use the **objective case **of a **pronoun **when it is used at the **place of the object**.
 
 
• ​​Example: 
 
 
• **I** know him very well. *(**subjective case**)
 
• *He knows **me **very well.* (**objective case**)
 
 
 
 
 
• *​*So to make the sentence correct replace the *subjective case* '**I***'* with the *objective case *'**me**.' 
 
• Thus *option 2 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *These tutorials are so elementary that they can help neither you nor **me**. * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn more about the **subjective **and the **objective case**.

 
 
• The *subjective case *is the case used for a noun or pronoun that is the **subject of a verb**. Whereas, the *objective case *is the case used for a noun or pronoun that is the **object of a verb**

 
 
• **Example: **

 
 
• ***I** saw the dog. *(**subjective case **of the pronoun *I*)
 
• *The dog saw **me**. *(**objective case **of the pronoun *I*)
 
 
 
 
 
 

ac:T
